summary.text: Acting for Folake Adeyemi (claimant), this brief addresses 1 issue(s) arising from Adeyemi v Harbourside Hotel Ltd: Ms Adeyemi wants to recover the value of her stolen property and argues that the notice excluding liability is not part of her contract with the hotel.
Can Harbourside Hotel Ltd rely on the exclusion clause: was it incorporated into the contract and does it cover the loss? Finely balanced for Folake Adeyemi.

facts.text: On 12 August 2025 Ms Adeyemi arrived at the Harbourside Hotel without a booking and asked for a room at the reception desk.

At reception she signed a registration card recording her name, address and car registration. The card contained no terms and conditions and did not refer to any. She paid for two nights and was given a key card.
A notice on the back of her bedroom door stated: "The hotel accepts no liability for loss of or damage to guests' property left in rooms. Valuables must be deposited at reception."
The same terms appear on the hotel's website, which Ms Adeyemi had never visited.

On 13 August 2025, while she was at dinner, her laptop and a diamond bracelet worth £6,500 in total were stolen from her room. The police found no forced entry; a member of staff had left a master key card unattended on a cleaning trolley.
The hotel relies on the bedroom notice to exclude liability and says Ms Adeyemi should have deposited her valuables at reception.

issues.question: Can Harbourside Hotel Ltd rely on the exclusion clause: was it incorporated into the contract and does it cover the loss?

proposition.text: Terms must be brought to a party's notice before or at the time the contract is made; a notice first seen after the contract has been concluded is not incorporated.

supporting_precedents.case_name: Parker v South Eastern Railway Co

proposition.text: Unsigned terms on a ticket or notice are incorporated if the party relying on them took reasonable steps to bring them to the other party's attention before or at the time the contract was made.

supporting_precedents.case_name: Thornton v Shoe Lane Parking Ltd

proposition.text: Terms referred to on a ticket issued after the contract is concluded are not incorporated, and the more onerous or unusual a clause is, the more clearly it must be brought to the other party's attention.

opposing_precedents.case_name: Photo Production Ltd v Securicor Transport Ltd

proposition.text: In commercial contracts between parties of equal bargaining power who allocate risks, including by insurance, a clearly worded exclusion or limitation clause will be given effect according to its true construction.
A party who signs a contractual document is bound by its terms in the absence of fraud or misrepresentation, regardless of whether they read them.

Valuables must be deposited at reception.".
